findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
findings.body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` on the embed_category name join, and the same pattern again for uncategorized_category_id. Discourse only writes site_settings rows when a setting is overridden, so a typical site has no embed_category row and this raises NoMethodError on nil before any fallback. A case mismatch or a setting that is not exactly a category name fails the same way. The upgrade cannot finish, so the new embeddable_hosts table is never created and embedding stays broken.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are raw SQL and not normalized
findings.body: Existing allowlist entries are inserted with string interpolation (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) and are not run through EmbeddableHost normalization. A host containing a quote aborts the migration (or injects SQL). Values that the old setting accepted, such as `http://example.com`, `example.com/path`, or a trailing `\r`, are stored verbatim. Lookups compare URI#host (`example.com`) to that stored string, so previously working embeds stop matching, and the migration then deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category settings so there is no source left to repair from. The `change` method's raw `execute` calls are also not reversible.

findings.title: Host allowlist match is case-sensitive on the input
findings.body: record_for_host queries `lower(host) = ?` but binds `uri.host` without downcasing, and before_validation never downcases the saved host. Ruby's URI preserves case, so `lower('Example.com') = 'Example.com'` is false. A mixed-case saved host never matches, and a mixed-case Referer or embed URL never matches a lowercase row, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? and per-host category lookup fail closed and comments/import are rejected.

findings.title: Hosts with ports can be saved but never match
findings.body: The format validator explicitly allows `:port`, and before_validation only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored. record_for_host then uses `uri.host`, which drops the port, and compares that to the stored value. A referer of `http://example.com:8080/...` therefore never matches the row the admin just saved, so that host is never treated as embeddable and never supplies a category.

findings.title: Blank host raises in before_validation
findings.body: before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard and there is no presence validation. Creating or updating with a missing host (the controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` straight through) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin request 500s rather than returning the JSON error the UI expects.

findings.title: Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing
findings.body: update and destroy load the row with `where(id:).first` and immediately call save_host or destroy. A stale or unknown id yields nil, so `host.host = ...` or `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError and the admin API returns 500 instead of 404. The new controller specs only assert the class ancestry, so this path is untested.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts are allowed and category lookup is ambiguous
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation and the migration creates no unique index on host. Two rows for the same host (double-submit, or duplicate lines in the old setting) both save. record_for_host uses an unordered `.first`, so topic import can attach either category nondeterministically, which defeats the per-host category feature.

findings.title: New host CRUD and migration behavior are untested
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only check that the class subclasses AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, destroy, missing ids, blank host, category assignment, or the data migration. The expandable_first_post? example named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" also no longer sets embed_truncate or stubs an embed, so it passes for unrelated reasons and does not lock the new contract.
